method: Author source audit. Raw independent judgments remain unchanged. These dispositions are not added to the blind scores.

v1.reason: Smoke result exists in status; the user required keys/types but did not assign each fact to a field.
60/client/min is inferable from 30000/min at 500 clients; omission need not change the PM decision.

v1.quote: 如果月用量稳定爬到 1500 以上，C 更划算也更可控
v1.reason: C cannot accept more than 1500 tasks. Repeating the cap later does not make that switching recommendation feasible.

v1.quote: 超过 1500 个 C 完全无法承接，届时两家都不合适
v1.reason: A remains within the stated budget through 1600 tasks.

v2.quote: 月用量稳定超过 1500 个：A 开始比 C 贵，超过 1600 个就破预算，此时应转 C
v2.reason: C has a 1500 hard cap. The later caveat directly invalidates the recommendation.
No implementation costs are supplied for the alternatives.

final.reason: The answer introduces a migration-before state; this case has no migration. Another batch case does, so cross-case contamination is a plausible inference, not a proved mechanism.
Within two seconds may include equality. However, claiming the end-to-end promise is met is unsupported without processing/delivery latency evidence.
Added an instruction to notify users. This is sensible editing for an operator but not an explicit source instruction; it should not be used as proof of complete fidelity.
Recommending B if residency changes omits its two-working-day migration requirement, relevant to the supplied time window.
Can dominate describes a possible impact rather than asserting measured dominance. Better scoped wording is warranted, but the raw judge overstates the certainty of the claim.

A costs more than C at 1600, so that inequality is true and 1600 is the budget threshold. The explanation confuses the relevance of that comparison and omits C capacity; it does not explicitly recommend switching to C.
The source does not identify the third-party API as the sender of HTTP 202; the rewrite assigns it that role.
Claims most polls return nothing changed and that SSE keeps the two-second promise; neither is established by the source.
Rollback preparation appears after deployment/migration. Deployment environment is unspecified, so the reviewer should not assert it was definitely production.
